coordinates.locator: area centroid of OpenStreetMap way 191447189 ('Reactor Hall', ref ILL 5; element version 6, last edited 2025-08-17, read from the OSM API on 2026-10-28)
coordinates.note: Campus-grade point at the reactor hall, shown as approximate: the OSM outline (traced from the French cadastre) of the 60 m cylindrical reactor building. The Ricochet detector's own paper gives only its distance from the reactor core (8.8 m), not an absolute coordinate, so the exact detector position inside the hall is not sourced.

name: ILL Grenoble reactor hall
notes: The Ricochet detector sits 8.8 m from the ILL reactor core (arXiv:2208.01760); no separate, more precise detector-hall coordinate was found in a fetched source, so this campus-level point is used for the site record.

summary.plain: The research-reactor building at the Institut Laue-Langevin in Grenoble, France, where the Ricochet experiment sits about 9 metres from the reactor core to catch its antineutrinos.
summary.technical: Reactor hall of the ILL research reactor (58 MW thermal power), Grenoble, France; hosts the Ricochet CEvNS detector array 8.8 m from the reactor core.
